title: Designing to Control Heat Transfer
seo_title: Grade 6 Heat Transfer Worksheets: Conduction, Convection, Radiation and Insulators
standard_text: Apply scientific principles to design, construct, and test a device that either minimizes or maximizes thermal energy transfer.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on heat transfer (NGSS MS-PS3-3): conduction, convection and radiation, conductors and insulators, and testing cup, cooler and solar oven designs. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Heat moves by conduction, convection and radiation.
key_sub: Insulators slow heat transfer and conductors speed it up. Engineers use them to design coolers, thermoses and solar ovens.
body_html:
How to think about it

Thermal energy always moves from warmer to cooler objects, in three ways:

  • Conduction: between objects that touch (a spoon in hot soup).
  • Convection: carried by moving liquids or gases (warm air rising from a heater).
  • Radiation: as light or infrared waves, even through space (sunlight).

Conductors (metals) transfer heat quickly. Insulators (foam, wool, trapped air) slow it down. Engineers use these ideas to design coolers, thermoses, solar ovens and warm houses, and they test designs against criteria and constraints.

Example

A spoon in hot cocoa gets hot. Which kind of transfer?

The spoon touches the cocoa.

Answer: conduction

Example

Which keeps ice frozen longer: a metal box or a foam box?

Foam is an insulator.

Answer: the foam box

Common mistakes

  • Saying cold flows into things. Heat flows out of warmer things.
  • Thinking insulators make heat. They only slow heat transfer.
  • Thinking metal is colder than wood at the same room temperature.

faq.q: What are conduction, convection and radiation?
faq.a: Conduction is heat transfer by touching, convection is heat carried by moving liquids or gases, and radiation is heat carried by light or infrared waves.
Materials that slow heat transfer, like foam, wool, cork and trapped air.

faq.q: Why does a metal spoon get hot in soup but a wooden spoon does not?
faq.a: Metal is a good conductor, so heat moves through it quickly. Wood is an insulator.

items.q: In which direction does thermal energy always move?
c: from warmer objects to cooler objects
items.e: Cold does not flow; heat does.

items.q: Why does a thermos keep soup hot?
c: Its vacuum layer and shiny lining slow conduction, convection and radiation.
items.e: A good design slows all three kinds of heat transfer.

items.q: Mia observes sunlight warming your face. Which kind of heat transfer is this mainly?
items.e: Energy travels as light or infrared waves, even through empty space.

items.q: Emma's teacher asks for an example of conduction. Which is the best example?

a metal spoon getting hot in a pot of soup
a sea breeze blowing toward land on a sunny day
items.e: Energy moves between objects that are touching.

items.e: Energy travels as light or infrared waves, even through empty space.

items.q: What is an insulator?

a material that slows the transfer of thermal energy
items.e: Foam, wool and air are good insulators.

items.q: What are the three ways thermal energy is transferred?
items.e: These three processes move thermal energy.

items.q: Why are double-pane windows better at keeping a house warm?
